message: In risky work the developer fixes answer keys in another session, but nothing tells the main session to wait before recording the answer-key SHA.
Step 9 says to check out "that commit" to restore the answer keys, but that refers to the yolo-review fix commit, which comes after the step 8 deletion and no longer has the folder.
Auto-merge armed while the PR is two-way stays armed if a later fix push makes it one-way-door.
Importing only existing modules does not keep tsc clean when tests use new props or not-yet-written named exports, which can stop /implement's preflight.
Leaving a criterion to the checker's unit tests conflicts with /implement step 2 where the checker must confirm every criterion is tested, and the exemption lives only in a commit message.
In risky work, the checker reports answer-key gaps to the main session that drives builders, weakening the hidden-test separation.
Builders can no longer edit any test, but /implement never assigns the checker to update existing tests the spec intentionally breaks.
Step 10 says walk scenarios 'on staging', but /pr adds the Preview Environment label, so the feature is on the preview link, not staging.
Step 9 restores only the answer-key folder, not helpers deleted with it, and in risky work the folder may never have been committed on the PR branch.

The ownerless carve-out covers every file under learnings/feedback/ and comes after **/CLAUDE.md and **/AGENTS.md, so last-match-wins makes a CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or any other file placed there unowned. The engine also always skips feedback/** from review, so such a file is never seen by agents or a code owner.
'The checker writes every test' with yolo-review as the one exception conflicts with skills where the main session writes or fixes tests.
Adding the Preview Environment label after pushing triggers a second full CI run because ci.yml runs on labeled with no filter.
Step 6 has the model hand-match changed files against CODEOWNERS instead of reading the tier label pr-guard already sets.
"run step 9 again" is ambiguous: line 8 uses "step 9 of /implement" for the same number, so a reader may re-run the wrong step.
The checklist says a one-way door is any path listed in .github/CODEOWNERS, but the file now ends with ownerless carve-out lines that are listed there yet are not one-way doors.

CLAUDE.md says a test inside a one-way-door folder is a one-way door too, but the new file-level owners leave their neighboring tests unowned. pagePropsHelpers.test.ts and the scripts/jest-shards/*.test.ts files sit next to owned files but match no owner line.
